items.title: Tesla Cybertruck’s End Is Near: Elon Musk Confirms Production Wind-Down
points: Elon Musk has confirmed that Tesla will wind down production of the Cybertruck at its Texas Gigafactory around the middle of 2027.
The announcement marks a major retreat for a pickup that Musk once expected to sell in huge numbers, but Tesla has not confirmed that Cybertruck production will stop permanently at every factory.
The Cybertruck is currently made only in Texas, and Musk has not said it will be transferred to another plant.
When Tesla unveiled the Cybertruck in November 2019, Musk presented it as a radical new electric alternative to America's conventional pickup trucks.
That number fell to approximately 20,237 in 2025, a decline of 48%.

items.title: Kanpur man killed as Thar rams his scooter and drags him along for 20 metres; driver flees
points: A 61-year-old LIC housing finance agent was killed after a speeding Thar rammed his scooter and dragged him for nearly 20 metres before crashing into the boundary wall of a house in Kanpur on Saturday night.
The victim, Santosh Singh Chauhan, a resident of Swaraj Nagar in Panki, was returning home on his scooter after shopping in Keshavpuram.
The accident took place around 8 pm near Gayatri Palace in Awas Vikas-3, Kalyanpur.
Vinod Kumar, a lawyer who witnessed the accident while riding home with his wife on a motorcycle, said the Thar approached from behind at around 100 kmph.
He fell under the vehicle and was dragged for nearly 20 metres, Kumar said.
The Thar then broke through the boundary wall of a garden outside Prof Kailash Chandra's house before crashing into the wall of an adjoining property owned by GST superintendent Anita Mahadevan.
The Thar, which had “Krishna Group” written on its rear, is registered in the name of Krishna Kumar, a resident of Gyan Villa in Panki.

items.title: Himachal Pradesh to set up first fish parlour in Bilaspur, offering live and fresh fish for sale
points: To promote fish marketing in Bilaspur district and ensure fish availability for both residents and tourists, the Himachal Pradesh Fisheries Department will establish a 'Fish Parlour' in the district, officials said on Sunday.

Operating in conjunction with the Himachal Pradesh Tourism Department's 'Lake View Cafe' near the Fisheries Awareness Centre near Bilaspur's ITI Chowk, the parlour will provide tourists an opportunity to try traditional Himachali fish dishes.
A team led by the Director-cum-Warden of Fisheries, Om Kant Thakur, inspected the proposed site, necessary infrastructure, and other arrangements required for setting up the Fish Parlour.
For the first time, the parlour will provide consumers with the option to purchase live and fresh fish.
The Tourism Department's cafe is already operational on the first floor of the same building.
The synergy between the Fish Parlour and the cafe will enable the provision of local and traditional Himachali dishes prepared from fresh fish to tourists and other visitors.

items.title: Man Arrested For Firing 14 Rounds At Neighbour Over Parking In Faridabad

The victim, identified as Paramjeet, a 42-year-old employee of a multinational company in Singapore, was allegedly shot dead by his neighbour following a dispute over parking and other minor issues on Friday night in Sector 21C, under the Surajkund police…
According to Surajkund Station House Officer (SHO) Prahlad Kumar, the accused, identified as Monu Sharma alias Mohan, allegedly opened fire at Paramjeet around 9-9:15 pm using his licensed pistol.
Following the shooting, the Faridabad Crime Branch Sector 30 team launched an operation and arrested the accused within a few hours.
SHO Prahlad Kumar said all crime branch teams were immediately activated under the directions of senior officers, leading to the accused's arrest.
Both the victim and the accused lived in the same building at house number 641 in Sector 21C.

items.title: Bombay High Court quashes CBI case against 4 former Jet Airways employees in PF bribery case
points: After the CBI completed its investigation and filed a charge sheet against them, the four petitioners approached the High Court in 2024 seeking quashing of the case against them.
They argued that Bamne’s number was shared by fellow Jet Airways employees who described him as a “private consultant” who helped them withdraw their accumulated PF.

They said they had not met Bamne in person and had interacted with him only by phone and paid him without knowing that he was an EPFO employee to facilitate the withdrawal of their accumulated PF and therefore could not be said to have paid illegal…
Justice Jadhav, however, held that there was nothing to indicate that the petitioners knew that Bamne was an EPFO staff member.

Besides, the judge said, Section 8 of the PC Act punishes paying illegal gratification for the improper performance of public duty or as a reward for such improper performance, and again, there was nothing to indicate that they had the requisite intention…

items.title: At Least 25 Seafarers Killed In Strait Of Hormuz Since War Began Says IMO
points: The International Maritime Organization (IMO), the UN agency for shipping, said that no fewer than 25 seafarers have lost their lives around the Strait of Hormuz since the US-Iran war started on February 28.
The figure was revealed after the IMO Council, which has 40 member states, ended its five-day meeting on November 6, 2026.
Secretary-General Arsenio Dominguez said that seafarers are still being killed and seriously injured, while others are abandoned and kept away from their homes.
The most recent death was of a crew member on the tanker Velos Sapphire that came under attack on November 5, as per reports.
Reports further said there were 130 attacks on commercial ships in the region until now; however, nothing was told about how many seafarers got injured or went missing.
The count stood at 22 in mid-September, as informed by the IMO then.
Sources: IMO (via TASS, APA, Trend), reports on the Velos Sapphire attack Seafarers in the thousands remain trapped in the Persian Gulf.

points: Severely damaged human remains have been found aboard a chemical tanker that matches the drone-hit Wine Trader, Bulgarian prosecutors have said.

items.title: Lawrence Bishnoi gang member Hari Boxer detained in U.S., extradition process underway
points: Hari Boxer (40), a resident of Chatarpura village in Kotputli-Behror district of Rajasthan, was allegedly operating criminal activities in India from abroad.

Lawrence Bishnoi gang member Harichand Jat alias Hari Boxer has been detained in the U.S. by the Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE), and efforts are underway to bring him to India, Rajasthan Police said on Sunday (November 8, 2026).

Hari Boxer (40), a resident of Chatarpura village in Kotputli-Behror district of Rajasthan, was allegedly operating criminal activities in India from abroad and played a key role in supplying weapons to the Lawrence Bishnoi-Rohit Godara gang.
He was involved in extortion threats and firing incidents in Rajasthan, Haryana, Punjab, Delhi, Madhya Pradesh and Maharashtra, including Mumbai and Pune, AGTF ADG Dinesh MN said.
More than 22 cases, including attempts to murder, extortion, Arms Act violations and organised crime, are registered against him in various police stations in Rajasthan.

items.title: UP Teen Brothers Strangle Woman Over Affair, Hang Body To Show It As Suicide
points: Two brothers in Uttar Pradesh's Bhadohi allegedly strangled their 21-year-old sister over her relationship with a young man and hanged the body to make it look like suicide, police said on Saturday.

Additional Superintendent of Police Shubham Agrawal said the body of Khushi Bind, daughter of Teras Bind, was found hanging at her house in Jakhaon village under the Gopiganj police station area on November 4.
The post-mortem report received on Friday established that she had been strangled before being hanged, he said.
Following the post-mortem findings, a case was registered based on a complaint filed by the victim's father and an investigation was launched, Agrawal said.
During questioning, Khushi's two younger brothers -- 18-year-old Suraj Bind and his 15-year-old sibling -- allegedly confessed to strangling her, the officer said.
The brothers told police that Khushi used to speak to a person over the phone, a relationship opposed by the family.

points: Justice Mehroz Pathan passed the order on November 3.

The police registered an offence under Section 75 and Section 296 of the BNS and under the Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Act, 2019.
The judge rejected the argument that Section 18(D) of the Act of 2019 is not made out because the complainant did not have a certificate of identity under the Act.
Section 5 provides a route to apply to the District Magistrate for a certificate.

points: A Jawaharlal Nehru University (JNU) student allegedly attacked a fellow student with a meat cleaver over his friendship with a woman student, leaving him with severe injuries, including loss of vision in one eye, police said.
The incident took place around 3 pm on November 5 in room 119 of the Barak Hostel on campus.
The victim, identified as Saurabh, a second-year language student, was attacked on Thursday by the accused, Ajay, who allegedly objected to his friendship with a woman student, they said on Saturday.
Ajay allegedly assaulted Saurabh with the cleaver, inflicting serious injuries to his head, face, hand and eye.
The woman student, who was friends with Saurabh, approached the police with a complaint following the incident.
Based on her complaint, the Vasant Kunj North police station registered an FIR on Friday under sections, including attempt to murder.
Deputy Commissioner of Police (Southwest) Amit Goyal said an FIR had been registered, and an investigation was underway.

items.title: Kerala High Court Slams Private Bus Drivers, Calls Them ‘Yamas On The Streets’
points: The Kerala High Court has strongly criticised the reckless driving of private buses in Kochi, describing some drivers as “Yamas on the streets”, a reference to the god of death.
Justice Devan Ramachandran made the remarks on November 6 after watching video footage of a private bus fatally hitting a young woman in Kakkanad.
She was returning from a fitness centre on November 4 when a private bus allegedly travelling at excessive speed struck her near Kuzhikkattumoola Junction in Kakkanad.
The driver was arrested, and the police registered a case under Section 105 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, which concerns culpable homicide not amounting to murder.

items.title: Nifty, Sensex log worst Samvat returns in 15 years. What lies ahead in 2083?
points: The BSE Sensex slumped 8% and the Nifty 50 shed 7% in Samvat 2082, putting them on course for their worst Samvat-year performance since Samvat 2067, when both headline indices declined over 17%.
The underperformance of Indian equities in Samvat 2082 is a reflection of the difference between economic growth and stock market performance, said Ankur Punj, managing director of Equirus Wealth.

While earnings prospects have improved after three difficult years, annual earnings-per-share (EPS) growth of 10-11% over the next decade seems realistic, according to Saurabh Mukherjea, founder and chief investment officer of Marcellus Investment Managers.
The Nifty Metal Index (22%) and the Nifty Pharma Index (21%) led the Samvat 2082 rally, while the Nifty FMCG Index (-18%) and the Nifty IT Index (-9%) brought up the rear.
Punj said Samvat 2083 could be a year of earnings-led recovery, with better-than-expected results from largecap stocks such as Reliance Industries, HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank and Larsen & Toubro.

items.title: From coal to crop: How coal gasification can strengthen India’s fertilizer security
points: India’s fertilizer security depends on manufacturing capacity as well as on the availability and cost of the feedstocks used to make essential nutrients.

With agriculture requiring reliable supplies of urea and other fertilizers, coal gasification offers a way to convert domestic coal into chemical inputs, diversify production routes, and reduce exposure to international supply disruptions.
During the last financial year, India imported urea and ammonia worth approximately US$8 billion.
This underscores the need to strengthen domestic feedstock production and reduce import dependence across the fertilizer value chain.
In May 2026, the Indian government approved a ₹37,500-crore policy to encourage the gasification of surface coal and lignite.
It supports the government’s plan to gasify 100 million tonnes of coal by 2030.
Thermal efficiencies of around 90 per cent have also been recorded.
Carbon capture is now being built into gasification systems, with reported efficiencies in the range of 80-90 per cent.

According to the Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB), an AQI between zero and 50 is considered 'good', 51 to 100 'satisfactory', 101 to 200 'moderate', 201 to 300 'poor', 301 to 400 'very poor', and 401 to 500 'severe'.

Force Motors has staged a strong recovery from its historical support zone of Rs 16,500-17,000, which coincides with a previous consolidation range.
The stock has reclaimed its 20 and 50 DEMA, signalling improving price momentum.
ICICI Bank is showing a strong bullish breakout on the weekly chart, with the latest candle gaining 7.30% and closing at Rs 1,500.
The stock has reclaimed its previous resistance zone around Rs 1,480-Rs 1,500, indicating improving buying momentum.

It should be noted that over the last decade, the Indian indices Sensex and Nifty 50 have ended higher for the last eight successive sessions.

So, in the last ten years, both Nifty 50 and Sensex have ended higher for the last eight straight sessions, and the key indices have ended higher on 8 out of 10 Muhurat Trading sessions in the last 10 years.
This means the decadal strike rate for both the Sensex and the Nifty is 80%, and market observers expect it to rise to 90%.

items.title: New Honda Avancier Hybrid SUV Teased, Global Debut Expected On December 1
points: GaadiWaadi - The upcoming model will introduce the company’s next-generation hybrid technology and a fresh design language Honda has released the first teaser of the new Avancier, an upcoming hybrid SUV expected to make its global debut on December 1, 2026.
The new model is reportedly being developed as a seven-seater and will sit above the CR-V in Honda’s international lineup.
It is expected to be manufactured in Thailand, with Australia and several Asian markets among its likely destinations.
Honda first used it for an Accord-based station wagon sold in Japan between 1999 and 2003.
The name returned in 2016 on a crossover SUV developed for the Chinese market.
The teaser keeps most of the SUV hidden, but there are a few interesting details.
The main headlamp units appear to sit lower down, giving it a split-headlamp arrangement.
The design creates a distinctive H-shaped signature, complemented by Honda’s new corporate emblem and Avancier lettering.

A decisive breakout above this range could open the way towards ₹6,741 and ₹7,464, while ₹5,180 remained an important positional support.

items.title: Rajasthan Board Releases 2027 Exam Schedule With Revised Paper Timings
points: The Rajasthan Board of Secondary Education (RBSE) will conduct the Class 10 and Class 12 board examinations 2027 from February 16.
Last year, the Rajasthan Board conducted the Class 10 examinations from February 12 to February 28, while Class 12 examinations were held between February 12 and March 11.
The Class 10 results were announced on March 24, with an overall pass percentage of 94.23%.
Girls recorded a pass percentage of 94.20%, compared with 93.63% among boys.
The board declared the results for Science, Commerce and Arts streams together on March 31.
More than eight lakh students appeared for the Class 12 examinations.
In November 2025, Education Minister Madan Dilawar announced plans to introduce two examination opportunities for Classes 10 and 12.
However, in March 2026, RBSE Secretary Gajendra Singh Rathore said that the proposal had been sent to the state government for approval.
